cause: 8 GiB CPU land cache kept every visited tile's GPU allocation alive; the single pool buffer is capped at 1 GiB by gpu.rs device limits, so it filled and new covers could not upload (owner log: countless 'mesh pool full (1024 MB)').
changes: PoolStore evicts least recently used unprotected GPU ranges when allocation fails at max size; CPU PooledMesh stays cached and re-uploads via prepare_pooled.
Protected each frame: drawn meshes, uploads, Frame::retain_pooled ids (every cached tile on the pyramid's visited cover, incl. fallback ancestors and prepared children).
Pool growth may grow partially up to the device max.
Working-set-full warning throttled to once per 120 frames.

native.route: lat -33.75 lon 97.4, loop 10 km -> 6300 km -> 350 km -> 10 km, 6 s holds, 3 s moves, 100 s (~3.7 loops)

fixed_build.warnings_when: one per loop during the fast zoom-out transient (selected up to 471)

native.captures_checked: visually: sharp continent at 6300 km, full mountain detail at 350 km, second loop

limits: First cold loop still streams from disk (32 MiB/frame budget); seconds of fallback on first visit are expected.
Allocator coalesces adjacent free ranges only; no compaction. Not needed in this run (tiles are ~2.1 MB, nearly equal).
If a single cover's working set exceeds 1 GiB, fallback tiles are drawn for its remainder.
